title: Course 4 — Automation & Integration
intro:
Automate your workflows and connect external tools.

Covers no-code automations, Python scripts, the API, webhooks, workflow orchestration with n8n, and AI-powered document extraction — around a warehouse receiving scenario.

build-the-linking-automation.title: Step 2 · Build the linking automation
build-the-linking-automation.instruction: Build an automation on Line items that links each new line to its product and document.
build-the-linking-automation.hint: On Line items: trigger “a new row is added”, two conditions (Product reference & Document reference not empty), then two Add links actions — one to Products (Reference), one to Documents (Delivery reference).
build-the-linking-automation.html: Build your first automation. On the Line items table, create an automation that links every new line to its Product and its Document by matching references — no links entered by hand. Choose Guide me to build it one stage at a time (each checked before the next), or Just check it if you’ve already built it.
build-the-linking-automation.successMessage: Your linking automation is complete — every new line will now find its product and its document on its own.

watch.html: Watch it work. Your rule is built, but nothing has set it off yet — so let's give it something. First open the Line items table so you can see it happen, then let the plugin bring in the delivery lines, as if your supplier had sent through a tidy list of what was loaded onto the truck. Keep an eye on the Product and Document columns as the lines land: neither is part of what the plugin writes, and both fill themselves in.
watch.instruction: Open the Line items table, then add the three delivery lines and watch the links fill in.
watch.successMessage: Both links filled themselves in, on lines you never touched. You didn’t automate this delivery — you built a rule that holds for every line that will ever enter this table, whoever puts it there.

created.title: Automation created
created.instruction: Add a new rule in the Automations editor and give it a name.
created.hint: The name field of the rule has to be focused out for it to exist
created.html: Create the automation. Open the Automations editor and add a new rule and give it a name, then click Check.

trigger.title: Trigger + guard
trigger.instruction: Trigger on “When a row is added”, with Product reference and Document reference both not empty.
trigger.hint: Set the conditions in the Trigger settings panel
trigger.html: Set the trigger — and guard it. Choose “When a row is added”, then add two conditions so it only runs on complete lines: Product reference is not empty and Document reference is not empty.

action:0.title: Link the product
action:0.instruction: Add an “Add links” action matching Product reference to a product’s Reference.
action:0.hint: Choose the Add links action, then the Product column it should fill
action:0.html: Link the product. Add an Add links action that fills the Product column: the line’s Product reference should equal a product’s Reference.

action:1.title: Link the document
action:1.instruction: Add a second “Add links” action matching Document reference to a document’s Delivery reference.
action:1.hint: The same action again, this time filling Document
action:1.html: Link the document. Add a second Add links action that fills the Document column: the line’s Document reference should equal a document’s Delivery reference. That completes your automation.

a-reviewer-for-a-short-delivery.title: Step 3 · A reviewer for a short delivery
a-reviewer-for-a-short-delivery.instruction: Let the plugin create a short delivery, then run your rule from the automation editor and verify.
a-reviewer-for-a-short-delivery.hint: Use Run now in the automation editor — no need to wait for the scheduled hour.
a-reviewer-for-a-short-delivery.html:
Give your rule something to find. A scheduled rule only shows what it is worth on a delivery that actually needs attention — so rather than have you stage one, the plugin does it: it creates a new delivery and one line received short of what was ordered. Your step-2 automation attaches the line on its own; the plugin waits until it has.

Then go to the Automations editor and press Run now on your reviewer rule — no need to wait for the hour you set. Come back and verify: what is checked is not that a reviewer is there, but that your automation, and not you, is the one that put it there.
a-reviewer-for-a-short-delivery.handoffNote: You’re done here — head back to the website to continue the course ↩

rewind-and-do-it-for-real.title: Step 4 · Rewind, and do it for real
rewind-and-do-it-for-real.instruction: Let the plugin take the seeded delivery back out, then receive it again from the app and let the AI read the note.
rewind-and-do-it-for-real.hint: The form is the second page of the Delivery check app — attach the photo and submit; everything else is read from the picture.
rewind-and-do-it-for-real.html:
Take the delivery back out. You have the chain — what you do not have is anything to feed it: that delivery is already in your base, lines and all. Let the plugin remove them, and the document with them, so the same note can arrive the way it really would. Your stock goes back to where it was too.

Then receive it for real: in the Delivery check app, open New delivery note, attach the photo of the delivery note and submit. Watch the reading, the extraction and the script do the rest — then come back and verify.

If the extraction goes off the rails, the plugin writes the delivery's lines for you — whole if it produced none, corrected if it got them wrong. What is checked is that the lines are back, never that the AI got them right on its own.
rewind-and-do-it-for-real.successMessage: The delivery is back — read off a photograph this time, with its lines linked by the rule you built in step 2.
rewind-and-do-it-for-real.handoffNote: You’re done here — head back to the website to continue the course ↩

see-what-seatable-sends.title: Step 5a · See what SeaTable sends
see-what-seatable-sends.instruction: Point your webhook at the test endpoint first, then let the plugin make a change you know the shape of.
see-what-seatable-sends.hint: Nothing is graded here — the whole exercise is to go and read what arrived at the other end.
see-what-seatable-sends.html:
Give your webhook something to say. With your webhook pointed at the test endpoint, the plugin will make a change you know the shape of: it adds a row to Products, edits it a few seconds later, then deletes it — leaving your catalog exactly as it was. Keep the test page beside your base: the three changes are spaced so you can watch each one land on both sides. If nothing reaches the endpoint, try moving both pages into the same browser window.

Three operations, three requests: what was written, what changed (with the value it held before), and what went. Nothing is checked here — reading the other side is the whole exercise.
see-what-seatable-sends.handoffNote: You’re done here — head back to the website to continue the course ↩
see-what-seatable-sends.demoDoneMessage: ✅ The three changes have been made — go and read them at the other end.

write-the-deliverys-lines.title: Step 5b · Write the delivery’s lines
write-the-deliverys-lines.instruction: Let the plugin write the second delivery’s lines, rather than copy three barcodes off a photograph.
write-the-deliverys-lines.hint: The lines land in Line items and your step-2 rule attaches them; then press Notify the dock on the document.
write-the-deliverys-lines.html:
Let the plugin do the typing. The second delivery note is in your base, and its lines are not. Copying three barcodes off a photograph teaches nothing, so the plugin writes them for you — the same lines a clean reading of that note would have produced.

They land in Line items carrying their references, so the rule you built in step 2 attaches each one to its product and its document as it arrives. Nothing is checked here.

Then finish the way the office finishes: read the list against the note, and press Notify the dock on the document.
write-the-deliverys-lines.handoffNote: You’re done here — head back to the website to continue the course ↩
write-the-deliverys-lines.demoDoneMessage: ✅ The delivery’s lines are in Line items, linked by your own rule.

the-electronic-delivery-note.title: Step 7a · The electronic delivery note
the-electronic-delivery-note.instruction: Let the plugin drop in the electronic delivery note, then go and push one of its lines from the API reference.
the-electronic-delivery-note.hint: Nothing is graded here — this only puts the note in your base so your pushed lines have something to link to.
the-electronic-delivery-note.html:
Play the supplier's system — the first half. One of your suppliers now generates its delivery note when the truck is loaded and sends it straight to your base. That conversation has two halves: the header of the note, then its lines. The plugin lays down the header, so that the half you do by hand stays small enough to read.

A new document appears in Documents with the reference {apiDeliveryReference} and no file attached — there is nothing to photograph any more.

Then it is your turn, back on the website: push at least one line into Line items from the API reference. Come back here at Step 7b when it is sent.
the-electronic-delivery-note.handoffNote: Now go and push one of its lines from the API reference ↩
the-electronic-delivery-note.demoDoneMessage: ✅ The delivery note is in your base, with no lines and no file.

check-the-pushed-line.title: Step 7b · Check the pushed line
check-the-pushed-line.instruction: Push at least one line into Line items from the API reference, then verify it arrived, linked itself and came in through the API.
check-the-pushed-line.hint: In the API reference, table_name is "Line items" and the row needs Document reference "{apiDeliveryReference}", a Product reference from your catalog, and a Qty.
check-the-pushed-line.html:
The second half is yours. From the API reference, push at least one line into Line items: the reference {apiDeliveryReference} in Document reference, a product from your catalog in Product reference, and a Qty.

What is checked is not only that your line arrived, but that it attached itself — to its product and to its document — through the automation you built back in step 2, and that it really came in from outside: a row typed into the grid by hand does not count here.
check-the-pushed-line.successMessage: Your line came in through the API and attached itself on the way — no scanner, no camera, no keyboard, and nothing in your base can tell the difference.
check-the-pushed-line.handoffNote: You’re done here — head back to the website to continue the course ↩
